# Maria Atamanova – mariascales.com

> Maria Atamanova – applied mathematician, twelve years growing businesses (apps, e-commerce, EdTech, AI data platforms): scaling growth and making it efficient on numbers, not gut feeling. Case studies, original research and interactive unit-economics tools. Senior Growth & Performance Marketing Manager (Praktika, Toloka, Scentbird, Buddy AI). Contact: hello@mariascales.com.

All pages are static HTML with en-dash typography and typed JSON-LD: Article, Dataset, SoftwareApplication, TechArticle, CollectionPage, HowTo, FAQPage, Person, BreadcrumbList. Research articles, case studies and dataset pages open with a TL;DR block carrying the main numbers; hub and index pages open with a “What is in here” block that does the same job under a different label; the two calculators lead with a summary paragraph and the design-decisions page with a contents list. Numbers on research pages come from the author's own datasets; sources and limitations are stated on each page.

- [Home](https://mariascales.com/): eight case studies with the numbers, the research series, and the two interactive tools, on one page.

## Tools

- [Tools](https://mariascales.com/tools/): hub - the two interactive models, what each answers and which is the subset of which
- [Unit Economics Estimator](https://mariascales.com/tools/unit-economics-estimator/): interactive subscription-app model – install-to-paid funnel, LTV M13, CPA, payback, target CPA; benchmarks from RevenueCat, Adapty, AppTweak and others, each input tagged B (benchmarked) / E (estimated) / A (assumption); 35 built-in self-tests
- [LTV Calculator](https://mariascales.com/tools/ltv-calculator/): the estimator's LTV engine alone – net LTV M13 by plan from a retention curve, VAT and store fee deductions, ROAS and payback against your own CPA
- [Design decisions](https://mariascales.com/tools/unit-economics-estimator/design-decisions/): why the model is built the way it is – discrete payment schedule vs the other LTV methods, retention power law, VAT handling
- [Benchmark snapshots](https://mariascales.com/tools/unit-economics-estimator/benchmarks/): every benchmark the estimator ships with, dated and sourced – 32 distinct inputs, 24 in the app funnel and 22 in the web funnel (11 B / 14 E / 7 A), 6 verticals, 6 geos, 18 public sources, downloadable as CSV; generated from the calculator's own constants

## Research

- [Research](https://mariascales.com/research/): hub - three series of original research: the marketing job market, automating a job search, and STEM education in the age of AI
- [Job boards are full of marketing. Most of it isn't.](https://mariascales.com/research/marketing-market/article/): 18,436 open postings from 590 company career pages (Jul–Aug 2026) – two thirds of "marketing" roles are sales; B2B 68% vs B2C 29% commercial; 83% of "remote" roles are single-country - two CSVs: the aggregates behind the 7 figures and the 88 classification rules
- [The Job Search Problem – Building a Reverse ATS](https://mariascales.com/research/job-search-automation/): series on partially automating a job search – ~65% sourcing overhead, the 7-second resume screen sources, 74% career-page probability, ATS public APIs (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday), an eight-table SQLite schema, 13 pitfalls
  - [The Job Search Problem – the framework](https://mariascales.com/research/job-search-automation/article/): Reverse ATS – deterministic filtering applied to postings instead of CVs; five structural problems of LinkedIn sourcing; two filters, ATS screening then a ~7-second scan; about 65% of active job-search time goes to sourcing
  - [Why sourcing takes ~65% of job-search time](https://mariascales.com/research/job-search-automation/65-percent/): structural floor 40–45% even with perfect search results; tracked 25-hour weekly cycle – 16.75 hours (67%) sourcing and filtering, 8.25 hours tailoring; 40% of companies posted a ghost job (ResumeBuilder 2023, 1,641 hiring managers)
  - [The 7-second resume screen – evidence and sources](https://mariascales.com/research/job-search-automation/7-seconds/): TheLadders 2018 eye-tracking study – 7.4 seconds average initial screen, the only hardware-measured source; job boards report 6–7 seconds
  - [Probability of a career page – the math](https://mariascales.com/research/job-search-automation/career-page-probability/): at least 74% of companies posting on LinkedIn have their own careers page – 25% × 40% + 35% × 75% + 40% × 95% = 74.2%; over 90% excluding micro-companies and Easy Apply; size-band probabilities are the author's estimates
  - [The Job Search Database – engineering the funnel](https://mariascales.com/research/job-search-database/article/): eight SQLite tables in two groups; 6 hard-stop rules and 18 position criteria as rows, not code; relevance_score of 1 or more enters the database
  - [Reading career pages without a browser](https://mariascales.com/research/ats-scraping/article/): public ATS JSON APIs instead of browser automation – Greenhouse ~30%, Workday ~25%, Lever ~15%, Ashby ~10% of a tech-heavy target list, the top four cover about 80%
  - [Potential pitfalls – problems and solutions](https://mariascales.com/research/pitfalls/article/): 13 pitfalls in 3 outcomes – 4 resolved by architecture, 4 solved by AI, 5 dismissed as edge cases
- [The Long Bet: STEM Education in the Age of AI](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/): 100 ARWU universities, 19 countries, 31 STEM programmes – CS at 95, standalone AI at 12; the four load-bearing A-levels (Mathematics, Further Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry); seven scarcity cycles in data and computing since the 1880s
  - [The problem statement](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/article/): a 17-year-old strong in mathematics choosing 4 A-levels; four constraints that do not resolve together; scope 100 ARWU 2025 universities, 19 countries, 31 STEM programmes, 5 datasets, June 2026
  - [How I built it](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/how-i-built-it/): ARWU over QS and THE; the top 100 as the cut; 1,200+ university–programme pairs normalised to 31 canonical labels; a 100 × 31 coverage matrix; Computer Science at 95 of 100 universities, standalone AI at 12
  - [What the world actually offers](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/what-the-world-offers/): Computer Science at 95 of 100, standalone AI at 12, a programme called “CS & AI” at 3; China 0 top-100 universities in 2003, 13 in 2025; France 4 top-100 universities, tuition ~€170 a year for EU students; UK 7 of 8 offer standalone AI, £30,000+ a year
  - [The unfashionable four](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/the-unfashionable-four/): Mathematics required by 30 of 31 programmes; Further Mathematics required by 2, recommended by 25; Physics required by all 12 engineering and physical-science programmes; Economics, Psychology, Business – 0 requirements
  - [The floor keeps rising](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/the-floor-keeps-rising/): the scarce skill in data and computing has shifted seven times since the 1880s; roughly 60 years of scarcity in the first era, about 4 in the current one
  - [The rising floor – the chart](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/the-floor-keeps-rising/the-rising-floor/): one stacked chart – eight columns, seven eras plus 2025→?, every layer a skill that was once the bottleneck; Domain Judgment as the unclaimed top layer, marked as a hypothesis
  - [The scarcity ladder – a timeline](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/the-floor-keeps-rising/the-scarcity-ladder-timeline/): seven eras plus a speculative eighth, each with the same three parts – what got democratised, what became scarce, who was elite
  - [ARWU Top 100 by Country, 2003–2025 – dataset](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/data/): every university in ranks 1–100 of the Shanghai Ranking, 23 editions, one CSV (2,303 rows) and one table – US 52 → 37 seats, China 0 → 13 all since 2016, UK 8 → 11 → 8, Germany 4 → 4
  - [STEM programme coverage, ARWU top 100 – dataset](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/data/programmes/): 1,258 university × programme pairs across 100 universities and 19 countries, 31 canonical programmes in 13 clusters; Computer Science at 95 of 100, Physics 94, Chemistry 92, Mathematics 91, standalone Artificial Intelligence at 12; 176 synonym pairs, two CSVs
  - [A-level requirements by STEM programme – dataset](https://mariascales.com/research/long-bet/data/a-levels/): 31 STEM programmes against 10 A-level subjects; Mathematics required by 30 of 31, Physics by 12, Further Mathematics required by 2 but recommended by 25; 9 of the 31 rows verified against live university admissions pages, 22 estimated; two CSVs

## Case studies

- [All case studies](https://mariascales.com/cases/): Praktika ($30M Series A, 5x revenue), Toloka (acquisition budget cut 66% vs the original baseline at flat revenue – 44%, then a further 22%; a separate 26% cut in major language segments; 65% retention lift), Scentbird (27% CAC cut while doubling Meta spend; 5% forecast accuracy), Buddy AI (32% LTV growth), a stealth subscription app (pixel overfit diagnosis)
- [Growth That Doesn't Lie to Itself: a ceiling mistaken for a floor](https://mariascales.com/cases/stealth/): stealth consumer subscription app, Meta - a ~$900k/month ramp stopped; 50+ concepts failed to reset delivery, only 2 worked on a clean pixel; pixel overfit diagnosed and proved
- [Praktika: marketing-led path to a $30M Series A](https://mariascales.com/cases/praktika/): revenue x5 while exceeding the profit KPI, $30M Series A closed in under 3 months, 50+ influencer collaborations; unit economy model per platform and geo
- [Toloka: unit economy model for media buying](https://mariascales.com/cases/toloka-unit-economy/): worker acquisition budget -44% at flat revenue (hypothesis was 30%), share of high-quality workers +21%; cohorts ranked by money-per-hour
- [Toloka: marketing-led product-market fit](https://mariascales.com/cases/toloka-pmf/): retention +65% (hypothesis was 10%), tasks per worker +21% after bonuses, labeling time -34% after prioritization, acquisition budget -26%, operations FTE -70%
- [Toloka: demand forecasting for request seasonality](https://mariascales.com/cases/toloka-forecasting/): 100% fulfillment on key big-tech requests, acquisition budget -22% at flat revenue; forecast from request-volume distribution by language
- [Buddy AI: worldwide user acquisition for a new startup](https://mariascales.com/cases/buddy/): LTV +32% (retention to recurring payment +29%, conversion to subscription +17%), LatAm scaled x1.5 at target ROI, Turkey launched
- [Scentbird: scaling user acquisition through operations](https://mariascales.com/cases/scentbird-ua/): CAC -27% and Meta spend x2 in 5 months at the ROI KPI; no-code automation alone -16% CAC, successful creatives x4 to 25%, FTE -13%
- [Scentbird: the business growth framework](https://mariascales.com/cases/scentbird-growth/): active user base +20% within months of the March 2020 lockdown, forecast model error 5% against a 7% target; budget split solved in Excel Solver on CAC-vs-volume curves
- [Pixel-overfit prevention framework](https://mariascales.com/cases/stealth/prevention-framework/): rules for validating audience breadth before scaling Meta spend

## Writing

- [Articles on HackerNoon](https://mariascales.com/articles/): paid acquisition measurement - baseline first, then the threshold a result has to clear: influencer spike of (baseline + volatility) x 2, LTV/CAC of 4 and 2 hours of daily routine before automating, 5% of budget before a creative counts as picked up
